# FMEA Database Mining — Technical Knowledge Library

> Public, versioned, source-traceable mining maintenance knowledge. This is a discovery index, not an API or certified knowledge base. Canonical data and limits are in the linked files.

- [Technical glossary JSON (67 terms)](https://pedromaintenance.github.io/fmea-database-mining/technical-glossary.v1.json)
- [Source discovery JSON (87 bibliographic items)](https://pedromaintenance.github.io/fmea-database-mining/source-discovery.v1.json)
- [Repository inventory snapshot JSON (500 paths)](https://pedromaintenance.github.io/fmea-database-mining/repository-inventory-snapshot.v1.json)

The glossary derives verbatim from the older author-controlled ontology and is pending technical review; the source listing is bibliographic, not proof of license or OEM serial applicability. The inventory is a pre-cycle snapshot and not an exhaustive semantic graph.

The atlas is a discovery aid, not an engineering endorsement. All subjects and bibliographic links require reading the canonical records; the hydraulic pilot is conceptual and not OEM validated by serial.

## V1.4.3: primary-source technical fundamentals
- [Human fundamentals portal](https://pedromaintenance.github.io/fmea-database-mining/fundamentos-hidraulica-tribologia.html)

- [Methodology and research audit](https://github.com/pedromaintenance/fmea-database-mining/blob/main/docs/CICLO_2026-11-07_FUNDAMENTOS_CAVITACAO_AERACAO_ABRASAO.md)

Cavitation, entrained air and abrasive wear are separate mechanisms. All three new articles are public, conceptual, pending independent review, and lack real field evidence, OEM serial effectivity and operational authority.

## Read before claiming technical facts
Public machine-family catalog specs are not OEM Test & Adjust limits. Synthetic reasoning exercises are not real failure events. A reference citation is not serial-specific effectiveness. Missing information is unknown, not zero, normal or safe. No automated SAP change, OEM approval or operational release.
